doc.title: Warren Vaché interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 23, 1995

chapter: Life on the road and advice
title: Life on the road and handling his own business
summary: He travels six to eight months a year, books himself without an agent, and supports a family.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Yeah. Tell us what a typical month for you is like now — a lot of traveling I would imagine, to get— I mean there’s probably not that many engagements right where you live.
I don’t think I’ve worked in New York in the last six years.

I’m on the road six to eight months a year. It’s a lot of traveling, a lot of flying. A typical month is basically spending a lot of time on the telephone trying to fill in holes in the calendar for the next month. I don’t very often get to control who I play with, but through these years I’ve developed a system of very dear friends, I don’t have an agent, so these friends will —
I was going to ask, so you handle your own business?

Well, yeah. I’m looking for somebody but it’s one of those catch-22 situations where you don’t make enough money without an agent to warrant an agent. You know I just am going to crack that wall one of these days. Well so far I’ve managed to make a fairly decent living and I do what I like to do so there’s a certain, I mean, I won’t be driving the Cadillac this year, I won’t be retiring at age 50, but I get to do what I like.
Ralph Sutton has an attitude that’s quite like that, and he seems to say I’m not going to do anything I don’t want to do. And I said, gee, that’s nice.

Well Ralph is in a situation and at a stage in his life where he can say that. Now I’m supporting a fourteen year old and an eight year old, an ex-wife, and myself. So much as I would like to say I’m not going to do anything I don’t want to do, very often the reality is get me something to do, you know?
